discovery: Proposal and realization of quantum computing and quantum simulation with trapped ions and neutral atoms

nominees.name: Ignacio Cirac
nominees.affiliation: Max Planck Institute of Quantum Optics, Garching, Germany

nominees.name: Peter Zoller
nominees.affiliation: University of Innsbruck and IQOQI, Austrian Academy of Sciences, Innsbruck, Austria

nominees.name: Rainer Blatt
nominees.affiliation: University of Innsbruck and IQOQI, Austrian Academy of Sciences, Innsbruck, Austria

subfield: Quantum optics and quantum information / atomic physics
motivation: In 1995 Cirac and Zoller showed how laser-cooled trapped ions could act as a scalable quantum computer: qubits stored in internal states, entangling gates mediated by shared motional modes. This was the first concrete physical blueprint for quantum computation. With Jaksch and others they then showed that neutral atoms in optical lattices realize Hubbard models, which launched analog quantum simulation. Blatt turned the ion-trap blueprint into reality. His group demonstrated the Cirac-Zoller gate, deterministic teleportation, multi-qubit entanglement, error-correction primitives and digital quantum simulation, which established trapped ions as a leading quantum-computing platform. Together their work founded the field of quantum information processing with atoms. Today it supports ion-trap and neutral-atom quantum computers and programmable quantum simulators worldwide. Their contribution moved quantum information from abstract theory to laboratory physics, a decisive turn that the 2012 prize honored only in part.
